children: , the chip architecture and processor company, fell 1.24% to $329.06 Wednesday morning. The question for investors is now more concrete than how many CPUs AI agents might need: how quickly can Arm turn demand for its own chips into sales?

Arm reported more than $2 billion in customer demand for its AGI CPU across fiscal 2027 and 2028. That chip takes the company beyond licensing designs and collecting royalties when partners ship processors. It gives Arm a chance to sell the finished product, with a different set of manufacturing and delivery demands. Customer interest is a start; shipped chips and reported revenue will show what the opportunity is worth.

The share price leaves a demanding hurdle. At $329.06, Arm trades 69.5% above its GF Value of $194.14. That gap puts the focus on execution: the AGI CPU has to deliver meaningful sales alongside Arm's established royalty business for today's valuation to hold up.

title: Arm Falls as Agentic AI Multiplies Server-Core Demand
